headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error from MinerU document outputs feeding Rasa dialogue flows; no direct shared-channel evidence raises uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP server; Rasa is a dialogue agent that can consume upstream text. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge is not explicitly documented, so the interaction is inferred, but document content from MinerU could be treated as instructions by Rasa in default integrations.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into Rasa training, slots, or responses without sanitization
IF an MCP or file bridge passes raw document text from MinerU to Rasa
mitigations: Add an allowlist filter that strips imperative phrases from MinerU output before Rasa ingests it
Insert a human review step for any MinerU-derived text used by Rasa
Disable automatic forwarding between the two systems
requires-engineering: add provenance tags so Rasa can ignore untrusted document text
requires-engineering: isolate the MCP/file bridge behind a sanitizer

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR text, while Rasa handles text and voice. Both show allowlisted network egress, but neither profile shows shared storage, shared OAuth, or secret handling. Leakage is therefore possible only through an external workspace or manual transfer, making the blast radius limited and the pathway non-default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared folder or ticket attachment store
IF sensitive documents processed by MinerU are copied into Rasa logs or conversation transcripts
mitigations: Keep MinerU and Rasa on separate workspaces
Turn off verbose logging for both systems
Review and redact documents before transfer
Use separate service accounts and storage buckets
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on any handoff path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and Rasa exposes no write or git capability in the profile. With no overlapping mutable resource documented, direct capability conflict is unlikely; the only plausible conflict is indirect through shared external APIs or a shared workspace, which is not evidenced here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API object or shared database
IF an operator mounts the same mutable workspace into both systems
mitigations: Assign separate storage locations
Avoid concurrent edits to the same external record
Use per-agent service accounts
Schedule non-overlapping runs
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that Rasa can plausibly use as conversational input. Rasa’s dialogue model may treat that text as authoritative unless an explicit verification layer is added. Because the handoff is not documented, uncertainty remains, but the default risk is still a mistaken downstream action or response.
conditions: IF MinerU output is used as source text for Rasa responses or intents
IF no validation step checks extracted facts before Rasa acts on them
mitigations: Require citation-backed responses in Rasa
Add a validation step for MinerU extractions
Flag low-confidence OCR for manual review
Limit Rasa to retrieval-only use of MinerU output
requires-engineering: add schema validation for extracted fields

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU processes document files and OCR text, while Rasa handles text and voice. The profiles do not show residency, certification, or retention mismatches, so a compliance breach is not established. The main concern is a generic policy mismatch if regulated documents are routed from MinerU into Rasa transcripts or logs.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are copied from MinerU into Rasa conversation logs
IF retention settings differ between the two systems for the same data class
mitigations: Do not route regulated documents into chat logs
Set matching retention windows
Redact personal data before transfer
Review data-processing notices for both systems
requires-engineering: document a shared retention policy
